added_models.model: MC38 colon carcinoma in human PD-1 knock-in (humanised-PD-1) mice dosed with the product antibody itself: camrelizumab (SHR-1210) alone and with an IDO inhibitor (Tu 2019), and toripalimab at 0.3-10 mg/kg i.p. twice weekly (FDA BLA 761240 Study TR003)

efficacy.model: MC38 colon carcinoma in human PD-1 knock-in (humanised-PD-1) mice dosed with the product antibody itself: camrelizumab (SHR-1210) alone and with an IDO inhibitor (Tu 2019), and toripalimab at 0.3-10 mg/kg i.p. twice weekly (FDA BLA 761240 Study TR003)
efficacy.note: Product-dosed humanised-PD-1 MC38 model: camrelizumab (2019) and toripalimab 1-10 mg/kg (BLA 761240, 2023); its only SCLC tests are combination trials.
efficacy.short: Product-dosed knock-in MC38; only combination trials
efficacy.quote: In the MC38 xenograft model in hPD-1 transgenic mice, 25 in combination with the anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody (SHR-1210) achieved a synergistic antitumor effect superior to each single agent.
efficacy.confidence_note: Tu 2019 read at abstract level (PMC6580535 exists, not read); the hPD-1 'transgenic' line is not named, so identity with the exon-2 knock-in used for toripalimab is by system type, and the abstract gives no single-agent number for SHR-1210. Toripalimab Study TR003 predates the 2018 NMPA approval but has no public date before the 2023 FDA review (bundle lines 4447-4464). Cheng 2025 (PMID 39541202) read at abstract level; NCT04012606 has no posted results (checked 2026-11-06); NCT03417895 results posted 2024-08-07.
efficacy.reason: Combination trials; model dosed antibody alone
efficacy.judgement: Split from mc38-mouse-pd1-blockade under this run's track-identity rule: a product-dosed antibody in a humanised-PD-1 host is a different system from a rat-chimeric surrogate (4H2) in wild-type mice, and it makes a different prediction (the product itself works, not just the mechanism). Camrelizumab (Tu 2019) and toripalimab (FDA 2023: 'Administration of toripalimab to MC38-bearing KI mice i.p. twice weekly at 0.3, 1, 3, or 10 mg/kg resulted in treatment-related decreased tumor growth at doses >= 1 mg/kg') are pooled on one track as the same system with the same prediction; model_src names the FDA review as the filed record of the system and model_filed is true on that account. No existing entry re-keys: the three mc38-mouse-pd1-blockade entries (2014 untested, 2016 same, 2020 contra) are all the nivolumab 4H2 surrogate; on merge, drop the clause 'later pooled with toripalimab's MC38 in human PD-1 knock-in mice' from that track's model text and the pooling sentence from its 2014 judgement. Status untested: the model dosed the antibody alone (Tu 2019's partner was an IDO inhibitor, not chemotherapy or apatinib; TR003 had no chemotherapy arm), and both SCLC tests are combinations, EXTENTORCH (toripalimab plus etoposide-platinum vs placebo plus etoposide-platinum, PFS and OS met) and PASSION (camrelizumab plus apatinib, single-arm ORR 34 %), so under this run's combination rule neither credits the model; both are recorded in patient_trials and change no status. Reviewer's call, as on the poppk-regimen-simulation track: a placebo-controlled add-on isolates the antibody, and under that reading this entry would be same (toripalimab, 2024). No dose entry is opened: the review does not set the model's >= 1 mg/kg threshold against clinical exposure, and the regimen question already sits on the poppk-regimen-simulation track.

patient_trials.quote: Compared with placebo, toripalimab improved investigator-assessed PFS (hazard ratio [HR], 0.67 [95% CI, 0.54-0.82]; P < .001), and significantly reduced the risk of death (HR, 0.80 [95% CI, 0.65-0.98]; P = .03).
In the QD cohort, confirmed ORR reached 34.0% (95% confidence interval: 20.9‒49.3), the median progression-free survival was 3.6 months, and the median overall survival was 8.4 months.

added_models.model: Rb1/Trp53/Msh2 (RPM) mismatch-repair-deficient autochthonous SCLC GEMM with high tumour mutational burden, dosed at MRI-confirmed tumour manifestation with the anti-mouse PD-1 antibody RMP1-14 alone or with cisplatin/etoposide, against the Rb1/Trp53 (RP) parental strain

efficacy.model: Rb1/Trp53/Msh2 (RPM) mismatch-repair-deficient autochthonous SCLC GEMM with high tumour mutational burden, dosed at MRI-confirmed tumour manifestation with the anti-mouse PD-1 antibody RMP1-14 alone or with cisplatin/etoposide, against the Rb1/Trp53 (RP) parental strain
efficacy.population: MMR-deficient, high-TMB SCLC (about 15 % of cases per the paper), with the unselected RP strain as comparator
efficacy.note: Opens the track: an Msh2-deleted RP mouse built to carry the MMR signature and high TMB that about 15 % of human SCLC shows.
efficacy.quote: RPM tumors exhibited MMR deficiency, high tumor mutational burden (TMB), and an elevated load of candidate neoantigens, compared to RP lesions (p = 0.0106), suggesting increased immunogenicity.
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC11564195; J Cancer Res Clin Oncol 150:496, epub 2024-11-14, PMID 39542886). The opener and the comparison are the same paper and year; the opener is kept so the track starts untested as the brief asks.
efficacy.judgement: Its own track: an autochthonous, MMR-deficient GEMM making a patient-level prediction (which SCLC responds) is a different system from the RP-48 OVA/LLO syngeneic flank model (sclc-rp-syngeneic-mouse, class-level) and from the sequencing-derived TMB rule (sclc-tmb-rule, no animal). The anti-PD-1 is the rodent surrogate RMP1-14 (product_in_model false); no regulator filed it.

efficacy.model: Rb1/Trp53/Msh2 (RPM) mismatch-repair-deficient autochthonous SCLC GEMM with high tumour mutational burden, dosed at MRI-confirmed tumour manifestation with the anti-mouse PD-1 antibody RMP1-14 alone or with cisplatin/etoposide, against the Rb1/Trp53 (RP) parental strain
efficacy.magnitude_basis: anti-PD-1 alone: median survival 51.5 vs 41 days in RPM mice (p = 0.0422) and no survival effect in RP mice, vs the higher nivolumab response and survival in the high-TMB tertile of CheckMate 032 (Hellmann 2018); no common quantity
efficacy.population: MMR-deficient, high-TMB SCLC (about 15 % of cases per the paper), with the unselected RP strain as comparator
efficacy.note: Built after CheckMate 032's TMB analysis: anti-PD-1 alone extends survival only in the high-TMB RPM mice, not in RP mice, reproducing the TMB rule.
efficacy.short: High-TMB SCLC mouse reproduces TMB rule
efficacy.quote: This notable response rate, which could be attributed to the elevated mutational load, aligns with recent clinical data indicating that high TMB bolsters the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibition in SCLC patients
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC11564195). The quoted sentence ends with the citation '(Hellmann et al. 2018)', omitted here. The paper summarises Hellmann 2018 in its introduction as benefit from 'a combination of two ICI agents' and in the discussion as checkpoint inhibition generally; Hellmann 2018 also reports the TMB effect for nivolumab alone, which is the member datum credited (the model dosed anti-PD-1 alone). Hellmann's tertile numbers were not re-read here; the patient-side quote is the draft's checker-verified abstract sentence. The paper itself cautions that clinical evidence for TMB as an ICI predictor is 'insufficient and contradictory' and that its regimens 'do not comply with standard clinical practice'.
efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction (decision 10): the model was built and run after Hellmann 2018 (CheckMate 032 TMB analysis) and Owonikoko 2021 (CheckMate 451 prespecified TMB subgroup), and the paper opens from Hellmann, so retro, never same. The comparison is stated by the paper (comparison_stated true, source_calls_it match). Patient-level: the prediction is that MMR-deficient / high-TMB SCLC benefits from anti-PD-1 while unselected SCLC does not, which is the sclc-tmb-rule track's rule re-derived in a mouse; it also reproduces the class-level monotherapy inertness (ICI alone did nothing in RP mice) that the sclc-rp-syngeneic-mouse track scores. endpoint_role primary with a caveat: the patient side is CheckMate 032's retrospective TMB analysis of its ORR primary endpoint, not a prespecified test. The combination arm is not scored: anti-PD-1 plus cisplatin/etoposide 'did not outperform chemotherapy alone' in RPM mice, the authors attribute that to toxicity, the only member combination trial (EXTENTORCH, toripalimab, unselected patients) went online the same day this paper did and is not a high-TMB datum, and the paper names only atezolizumab and durvalumab (non-members) for chemo-immunotherapy. First prospective test of this model's prediction would be a fresh entry.

added_models.model: Rb1/Trp53/p130 (RPP) GEMM-derived syngeneic SCLC flank tumours in immunocompetent B6129F1 mice dosed with an anti-mouse PD-L1 antibody, alone and with PARP or CHK1 inhibitors (Sen 2019) or the WEE1 inhibitor adavosertib (Taniguchi 2022, which adds an Rb1/Trp53/MycT58A line)

efficacy.model: Rb1/Trp53/p130 (RPP) GEMM-derived syngeneic SCLC flank tumours in immunocompetent B6129F1 mice dosed with an anti-mouse PD-L1 antibody, alone and with PARP or CHK1 inhibitors (Sen 2019) or the WEE1 inhibitor adavosertib (Taniguchi 2022, which adds an Rb1/Trp53/MycT58A line)
efficacy.note: SCLC-genotype immunocompetent mouse dosed with anti-PD-L1, a sibling target outside the class; alone it was inert, as in the clinic, but no member was dosed.
efficacy.short: Anti-PD-L1 in SCLC mice; sibling class
efficacy.quote: PARP or CHK1 inhibition remarkably potentiated the antitumor effect of PD-L1 blockade and augmented cytotoxic T-cell infiltration in multiple immunocompetent SCLC in vivo models.
efficacy.confidence_note: Sen 2019 (Cancer Discov 9:646, epub 2019-02-18, PMID 30777870) read at abstract level: Europe PMC did not serve the PMC6563834 full text. Taniguchi 2022 (Cell Rep 39:110814, PMID 35584676) full text read: 'Treatment with anti-PD-L1 antibody alone was not efficacious in this model.' Neither passage read names the anti-PD-L1 clone.
efficacy.judgement: Recorded untested with the rule conflict stated, as the caller allowed: decision 12 (#69) scores a sibling-class surrogate dosed in the model as other, but decision 13 and lint make other safety-only, so in the efficacy cell this track cannot carry a status. What the model showed, anti-PD-L1 alone not efficacious in RPP tumours (Sen 2019, Taniguchi 2022), runs in the direction of CheckMate 032/331's monotherapy inertness, and Sen opens from 'only a minority of patients with SCLC respond to immune checkpoint blockade', so if the class boundary were widened to the PD-1/PD-L1 axis this would be a retrodiction (retro), not same. A separate track from sclc-rp-syngeneic-mouse (RP-48 OVA/LLO in C57BL/6 dosed with anti-PD-1), whose own judgement excludes Sen 2019 from opening it. The combination partners (PARP, CHK1, WEE1 inhibitors) have no SCLC trial result with a class member. Reviewer may delete the track if sibling-class systems are to be left out of efficacy entirely; the alternative is in considered_not_added.

added_models.model: Mycobacterium tuberculosis aerosol-infected PD-1 knockout (C57BL/6) mice read for survival, lung bacterial burden and inflammatory cytokines against wild-type controls; carried into the Opdivo label section 13.2

safety.magnitude_basis: mouse: markedly reduced survival and uncontrolled lung bacterial growth after aerosol Mtb in PD-1 knockouts; patients: 5 tuberculosis cases (4 reactivations within 3 months) on nivolumab or pembrolizumab, about 1 per 1000 treated; no common quantity
safety.population: Unselected (imported: metastatic NSCLC in 3 of 5 cases, plus melanoma and Hodgkin lymphoma)
safety.confidence_note: Full text read via ScienceDirect scrape (Clin Microbiol Infect 24:216-218, epub 2017-12-18, print 2018-03, PMID 29269089). Case series of 5 (2 REISAMIC registry cases, 3 from the literature), no SCLC patient; the authors note reactivation could also stem from the cancer and prior chemotherapy. No registry record applies. Patient-side reports are reactivation of latent infection, the mouse modelled primary aerosol infection.
safety.model: Mycobacterium tuberculosis aerosol-infected PD-1 knockout (C57BL/6) mice read for survival, lung bacterial burden and inflammatory cytokines against wild-type controls; carried into the Opdivo label section 13.2
safety.note: Imported from NSCLC, melanoma and lymphoma: five tuberculosis cases on nivolumab or pembrolizumab, mostly reactivation within 3 months, the infection harm PD-1 knockout mice had foretold.
safety.quote: Moreover, the five cases reported here show that an anti-PD1 agent per se might favour tuberculosis reactivation.
safety.judgement: Scored same under the safety transfer rule with imported_from NSCLC (3 of 5 cases; melanoma and Hodgkin lymphoma the rest): the knockout predicted that PD-1 loss worsens Mtb control, and patients on members developed tuberculosis. Partial and low confidence because the evidence is five uncontrolled cases, the human event is reactivation rather than primary infection, and the authors leave cancer and chemotherapy as alternative causes. Dated 2017 from the e-publication. Paired by us with Lazar-Molnar 2010; Picchi cites knockout mechanism data (Sakai 2016) but not this model's survival result.

considered_not_added: Picchi 2018 tuberculosis reactivation on anti-PD-1 (Clin Microbiol Infect, PMID 29269089): an imported safety comparison for the EXISTING mtb-infected-pd1-knockout-mouse track, not a missing system; left to that track's owner (would be same, imported_from the reported indication).

Toripalimab 26-week cynomolgus toxicology (FDA 2023 review: 100 mg/kg weekly NOAEL, 13-23-fold AUC margin over 240 mg Q3W): same system as the existing cyno-monkey-ro track; not a new system, and that track is already contra.

Toripalimab Study TR003 NSG mice bearing MC38 engrafted with allogeneic human CD8+ CTLs (FDA 2023 review lines 4434-4440, 'minor antitumor activity'): a one-off assay superseded in the same study by the knock-in model; no patient comparison found; not added.

Human-PBMC-engrafted mice (toripalimab T-cell expansion, FDA 2023 review line 4112) and Fu 2017 HBsAg-vaccinated cynomolgus PD-1 pharmacodynamics (Acta Pharmacol Sin, PMID 28317872): engagement-type readouts with no stated human comparison beyond the in-vitro occupancy track the draft already holds; not added.
99mTc-JS001 SPECT (PMID 31257084) and 124I-JS001 immuno-PET in humanised mice (PMID 32874831): tracer biodistribution, no prediction compared with patients; not added.
Rajasekaran 2024 toripalimab binding/potency paper (PMID 38400933): in-vitro characterisation, same system as the in-vitro-pd1-occupancy track; not added.
Junk 2021 human lung-cancer tissue cultures predicting checkpoint-inhibitor susceptibility (PMID 34564709): NSCLC patients, not SCLC; cross-indication transfers for safety only; not added.

SCLC patient-derived organoids, CDX/PDX or humanised-PDX dosed with a member drug: none found in the PubMed sweeps (hits were NSCLC); WebSearch/fc.py not run within budget, so this arm is unverified rather than excluded.

PASSION (Fan 2021, PMID 33166719, NCT03417895 results 2024-08-07): a camrelizumab plus apatinib combination trial, placed in patient_trials of the hpd1-knockin-mc38 track (camrelizumab is the product dosed in that model); changes no status.
